Nice spot for Turkish one
Jul 2025 • Friends
I’ve been eating at this spot since it was just a small setup in a house. It’s been great to see how they’ve grown,now in a new, bigger location and continuing to expand.

The food has always been good,authentic, flavorful, and satisfying. However, the service could use some improvement. It’s not terrible, but definitely not the most welcoming or attentive at times.

Prices are generally acceptable, though some dishes feel a bit overpriced for what you get. Also, be prepared to wait for a table during busy hours,it can get quite crowded.

Overall, it’s a solid place for Turkish food in the area, especially if you’re craving something different, but there’s room for improvement on the service side.

Nice Turkish Restaurant
Sep 2024 • Friends
Overall, it was a delightful experience. The balloon and pita bread were the highlights of the meal. The bread was freshly baked, soft, and warm, with the perfect balance of texture and flavor. It complemented the dishes wonderfully and left a great impression.

However, I have to mention that the original Istanbul Restaurant on Le Quang Dao Street seemed to offer a better taste overall compared to the newly opened location on Tran Phu. While both places serve similar dishes, the original restaurant had a richer, more authentic flavor that really stood out. The newer location, while still good, didn’t quite capture the same level of quality and taste.

That being said, Istanbul Restaurant still offers a great dining experience, and if you're in the area, it's definitely worth a visit, especially if you love freshly made pita and balloon bread!
